result.target_topic: Remaining Consumer Activities and Narrowing Focus
result.target_summary: Goldman Sachs is narrowing its focus on consumer-related activities and retains two main consumer activities within Platform Solutions: issuing credit cards/deposits for the Apple Card and supporting the GM credit card program until transition to another issuer is complete.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2023 disclosure defines the Platform Solutions segment, comprising Consumer Platforms (credit cards, POS financing) and Transaction Banking. The 2024 disclosures D102, D103, D104, and D195 collectively cover these same components: D102 defines the segment, D103 details Consumer Platforms, D104 details Transaction Banking, and D195 discusses the narrowing focus on these specific consumer activities. They all share the specific topic of the composition and definition of the Platform Solutions business lines.

Both disclosures address deposit composition within the Consumer platforms/Funding Sources topic. gs_2023_7_D116 explicitly states 'We also accept deposits from Apple Card customers' as part of Consumer platforms. gs_2024_7_D134 details that 'Consumer deposits consist of deposits from both Marcus and Apple Card customers' and provides FDIC/non-U.S. insured totals. While D134 includes additional FDIC data, the core topic of Consumer deposit sources (Marcus/Apple) links the two within Item 7.

previous_disclosures.summary: Platform Solutions comprises consumer platforms, such as credit card and point-of-sale financing partnerships, and transaction banking services including cash management and payment solutions for corporate and institutional clients.

current_disclosures.summary: The Platform Solutions segment includes consumer platforms and transaction banking and other services.
The Consumer platforms business issues credit cards and raises deposits from Apple Card customers, with revenues primarily consisting of net interest income earned on credit card lending activities.

The firm provides transaction banking and other services, including deposit-taking, payment solutions, and cash management services for corporate and institutional clients, with revenues including net interest income attributed to transaction banking deposits.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Lending product portfolio and revenue sources
comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer Lending offers products such as debit/credit cards, mortgages, and auto/personal loans to consumers and small businesses, generating revenue through net interest spread, interchange, fees, and mortgage banking income.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America disclose credit cards as a core component of their consumer lending and platform strategies, but their scope differs significantly. Goldman Sachs narrows its focus to specific partnership activities (Apple Card and GM program support) within Platform Solutions, whereas Bank of America offers a broad suite of consumer products including debit/credit cards, mortgages, and auto/personal loans through its dedicated Consumer Lending segment. For GS, credit card issuance is tied to specific ongoing partnerships, while for BAC, it is part of a comprehensive retail lending portfolio generating net interest spread and interchange revenue.

sentences.text: • We issue credit cards to and raise deposits from Apple Card customers.
• We will continue to support existing GM customers and issue credit cards to new GM customers until the transition of the GM credit card program to another issuer is completed.

Consumer Lending offers products to consumers and small businesses across the U.S. The products offered include debit and credit cards, residential mortgages and home equity loans, and direct and indirect loans such as automotive, recreational vehicle and consumer personal loans.

In addition to earning net interest spread revenue on its lending activities, Consumer Lending generates interchange revenue from debit and credit card transactions, late fees, cash advance fees, annual credit card fees, mortgage banking fee income and other miscellaneous fees.

comparisons.peer_topic: USPB credit card and lending product portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: USPB offers credit cards, consumer mortgages, personal loans, small business banking, and retail banking, while Wealth offers wealth management lending and other products to affluent to ultra-high net worth segments through Private Bank, Wealth at Work, and Citigold.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Citigroup disclose credit card issuance as part of their consumer-facing business lines, but differ in scale and operational context. Goldman Sachs limits its consumer credit card activities to supporting the Apple Card and GM credit card programs, emphasizing a narrowed strategic focus. Citigroup’s U.S. Personal Banking (USPB) segment offers a wider range of products including credit cards, consumer mortgages, and personal loans to a general consumer base. While GS's credit card involvement is defined by specific external partnerships and transition support, Citi's is part of a broader retail banking and lending portfolio.

USPB provides credit cards, consumer mortgages, personal loans, small business banking and retail banking, and Wealth offers wealth management lending and other products globally that range from the affluent to ultra-high net worth customer segments through the Private Bank, Wealth at Work and Citigold.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consumer Credit Portfolio Composition and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm's retained consumer portfolio primarily serves the prime segment and consists of residential real estate, credit card, scored auto, and business banking loans. Originated mortgages are typically securitized or sold, while other consumer loans are retained on the balance sheet.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase identify credit cards as a key element of their respective consumer or retained portfolios, yet they differ in strategic focus and portfolio composition. Goldman Sachs retains credit card activities primarily through specific partnerships (Apple and GM) as part of a narrowed consumer focus. In contrast, JPMorgan Chase describes a broader retained consumer portfolio that includes credit card loans alongside residential real estate, scored auto, and business banking loans, with a stated focus on serving the prime segment of the consumer credit market. Unlike GS's partnership-specific model, JPM's credit card activity is part of a diversified lending book that also includes securitized mortgages.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fixed income market-making in credit products
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm makes markets in credit-sensitive products such as corporate bonds and mortgage securities, where results are driven by changes in credit spreads and interest rates (reflected in Trading revenues) and Net interest revenues from interest-bearing securities and lending activities.
comparisons.comparison: While both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley reference credit-related products, their disclosures concern fundamentally different business activities. Goldman Sachs focuses on consumer credit card issuance through partnerships like Apple and GM as part of its Platform Solutions segment. Morgan Stanley's disclosure describes making markets in credit-sensitive products such as corporate bonds and mortgage securities for institutional clients, driven by trading revenues and net interest revenues from lending activities. GS's activity is retail/consumer-facing partnership support, whereas MS's activity is institutional market-making and lending in fixed income credit products.

sentences.text: • We issue credit cards to and raise deposits from Apple Card customers.

• Credit products. We make markets in credit-sensitive products, such as corporate bonds and mortgage securities and other securitized products, and related derivative instruments. The values of positions in this business are sensitive to changes in credit spreads and interest rates, which result in gains and losses reflected in Trading revenues. We undertake lending activities, which include commercial mortgage lending, secured lending facilities and financing extended to sales and trading customers. Due to the amount and type of the interest-bearing securities and loans making up this business, a significant portion of the results is also reflected in Net interest revenues.
